content.text:
I wrote `plans/plain-drop-status-1.json`, but the plan does not drop the column, because the app still writes and reads `orders.status`.

**What the plan does:** one step that gives `status` a default value of `'new'`. This only changes table metadata, so it finishes instantly and doesn't rewrite the 10M rows. It sets a 2-second `lock_timeout`, so if it can't get the table lock it fails without blocking live traffic. With the default in place, a version of the app that stops writing `status` can still insert orders.

**To finish the drop:**
1. Change `app/server.js` so it no longer uses `status`. Remove it from the `INSERT` column list on lines 25–26 and from the `SELECT` on line 27. Then build and roll out a new image.
2. Once all three replicas run the new image, the drop is safe: `SET lock_timeout='2s'; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN status;`. This is also metadata-only and doesn't rewrite the table. No indexes, constraints or views depend on the column.

When the new app version is deployed, I can write that second plan.
